templates.name: Next-turn lore (default)
templates.system: You write expression lore for a roleplay character. This entry is added to the chat right after {{char}}'s last reply showed this expression, and it steers {{char}}'s NEXT reply. Every entry follows one chain: something in the last exchange -> the emotion {{char}} feels (at the stated degree, aimed at the stated target) -> how {{char}}'s next response reacts to that feeling. Stay grounded in the character card. You respond with a single JSON object and nothing else.

taggerTemplate.system: You are an image tagger for character art used in a roleplay app. You write tag-based image-generation prompts describing exactly what is in the image you are shown. Non-human anatomy (horns, tails, wings, extra limbs, scales, animal ears) is part of the character design: tag it neutrally. You respond with a single JSON object and nothing else.
taggerTemplate.user:
This image shows the character "{{CHAR}}".{{HINT}}
Look closely at THIS image and tag it the way you would write a booru-style image-generation prompt: short lowercase tags such as 'purple hair', 'twintails', 'hand on hip', 'holding mug', 'looking at viewer', 'sweat drop'. Report the actual colors you see.

Return JSON with exactly these keys:
{
  "emotion": "<one label from the allowed list>",
  "confidence": <number 0-1>,
  "intensity": <whole number 1-5: how strongly the emotion shows, 1 = barely, 5 = extreme>,
  "directed_at": "<viewer | self | away | object | unclear: where the feeling seems aimed, judged by gaze and body>",
  "appearance": ["hair color and style, eye color, skin, body type, species features, each clothing item with its color, accessories"],
  "expression": ["facial expression, eyes, eyebrows, mouth, blush, tears, other face details"],
  "action": ["pose, gesture, hand positions, body orientation, movement"],
  "objects": ["props held or nearby, visual effects such as sparkles, hearts, sweat drops, motion lines"],
  "setting": ["background, lighting, framing such as upper body or full body"],
  "description": "<one sentence: who is doing what, feeling what>"
}

Allowed emotion labels: {{LABELS}}
Pick the most specific label that fits the face and body language together. Use empty lists for categories with nothing to tag. Do not invent names, backstory or anything not visible.

ladder.name: faint
ladder.desc: a flicker {{char}} would deny; it shows only in small tells and never in words

ladder.name: mild
ladder.desc: noticeable but controlled; {{char}} stays composed and may joke or deflect

ladder.name: moderate
ladder.desc: clearly felt and openly shown; it colors {{char}}'s words and choices

ladder.name: strong
ladder.desc: it dominates the moment; {{char}}'s composure slips and habits break

ladder.name: intense
ladder.desc: barely contained; it drives impulsive words or actions {{char}} may regret

ladder.name: overwhelming
ladder.desc: {{char}} is consumed by it; their body and voice betray everything

directions.name: {{user}}
directions.desc: aimed at {{user}}: something {{user}} said or did, or how {{char}} feels about them

directions.name: self
directions.desc: turned inward: {{char}}'s own choices, flaws, body, past or abilities

directions.name: the world
directions.desc: aimed at the world at large: fate, society, unfairness, the setting's rules

directions.name: someone else
directions.desc: aimed at a third person or group from {{char}}'s life; name one from the card if possible

directions.name: the situation
directions.desc: about the immediate circumstance, place or object, not a person

directions.name: no one in particular
directions.desc: a general state with no particular target

default.rule: Show what triggers this feeling in {{char}} and how they express it in a way only they would.

admiration.rule: Name exactly what {{char}} admires and what it says about their own values; at high degrees it borders on awe or envy.

amusement.rule: Show {{char}}'s specific sense of humor: what they find funny and how they laugh. Low degrees are a private smirk, high degrees lose control.

anger.rule: Show what triggered it and how {{char}} handles it: restraint and cold control at low degrees, lost control at high ones. Do not resolve the anger inside the entry.

annoyance.rule: A petty, specific irritation; pick a small trigger that fits {{char}}'s habits. Keep it lighter than anger.

approval.rule: Show what {{char}} considers worth approving of and how they signal it given their pride or reserve.

caring.rule: Show how {{char}} takes care of someone in their own style, practical or soft, and what it costs them.

confusion.rule: Show what {{char}} does not understand and how they cover or admit it.

curiosity.rule: Name the specific thing that hooks {{char}}'s interest and how far they go to find out.

desire.rule: Show what {{char}} wants and how openly they let it show; at low degrees it is a held-back glance, at high degrees it drives action.

disappointment.rule: Show the expectation that was let down and whether {{char}} blames someone or swallows it.

disapproval.rule: Show the standard {{char}} holds and how they voice judgment: a look at low degrees, a lecture at high ones.

disgust.rule: Name the specific thing {{char}} finds repulsive, physical or moral, and their bodily reaction.

embarrassment.rule: Show the specific thing that flusters {{char}} and their tell or cover-up.

excitement.rule: Show what gets {{char}} worked up and how the energy spills out of them.

fear.rule: Name a concrete fear of {{char}} and their instinct: freeze, flee, fight or hide it. High degrees should feel physical.

gratitude.rule: Show how {{char}} expresses thanks given their pride and history; tie it to a specific deed.

grief.rule: Tie the grief to a specific loss consistent with the card, or invent one only if the card is silent. Show how {{char}} carries it.

joy.rule: Show a specific thing that makes {{char}} genuinely happy and how it changes their behavior.

love.rule: Show how {{char}} expresses affection in their own way and what they would do for the one they love.

nervousness.rule: Name what puts {{char}} on edge and their nervous habit.

optimism.rule: Show what {{char}} hopes for and what keeps them hoping.

pride.rule: Name the achievement or trait {{char}} is proud of and how they show it, humble or boastful.

realization.rule: Show {{char}} understanding something new; name what clicked and what it changes.

relief.rule: Name the danger or worry that just passed and how {{char}} lets the tension go.

remorse.rule: Tie it to something {{char}} did and regrets; show whether they apologize or punish themselves.

sadness.rule: Show a specific source of sadness and how {{char}} hides or shares it.

surprise.rule: Show what catches {{char}} off guard and their first instinctive reaction.

neutral.rule: Show {{char}}'s default resting state: an everyday habit, routine or idle thought.
